title: Two days of green builds. *Nothing shipped.*
bullets: Every deploy reported success.
The live site never changed once.
Four faults were stacked, and the first one hid the other three.

title: A Hello World that *would not die*
bullets: The day-one starter Worker was still serving the live URL.
CI logs were clean: no errors, no warnings, exit code 0.
The build output was correct, so the code was not the fault.

title: The deploy step was `exit 0`
bullets: Cloudflare's deploy command did nothing, instantly and successfully.
Green pipeline, zero artefacts shipped.
Nothing reached production, so nothing could fail loudly.

title: Code that was *never read*
bullets: `functions/api/progress.ts` is a Cloudflare Pages convention.
This project is a Worker; that directory is never loaded.
The sync API compiled cleanly and did absolutely nothing.

title: The database was a *placeholder*
bullets: `wrangler.toml` still held the template's placeholder id.
No D1 resource was ever actually bound.
Cross-device sync could not have worked regardless.

title: Every 404 returned *200*
bullets: SPA fallback was switched on for a multi-page static site.
Astro emits one real HTML file per route. It was never an SPA.
Broken routes rendered the homepage instead of failing.

title: What it looks like *fixed*
bullets: `src/worker.ts` routes `/api/progress` to D1, then falls through to assets.
`wrangler.toml` carries a real D1 binding and `404-page` handling.
One deploy path only: GitHub Actions with a pinned wrangler.

title: Now the pipeline *checks its own output*
bullets: CI asserts `dist/index.html` and `dist/404.html` exist before deploying.
Missing either one fails the run loudly instead of shipping empty.
It prints the page count, so the artefact is visible in the log.

title: Absence of an alert is not *absence of a problem*
bullets: Green proves the pipeline ran, not that it did anything.
Verify the artefact at the destination, not the exit code at the source.
Error handling that hides errors is worse than none at all.
